requirements.requirement: Node1 runs an internal DNS resolver that resolves inventory-api.internal to node2.
requirements.summary: Node1 served DNS on TCP and UDP port 53, returned 10.100.144.11 for inventory-api.internal, and node2 confirmed that address as its own. Resolution remained healthy after node1 restarted.

requirements.requirement: Node2 uses node1 as its DNS resolver for internal lookups.
requirements.summary: Node2's active and persistent NetworkManager configuration names node1 at 10.100.144.10 as its resolver, and system resolution of the internal name succeeds. The configuration and lookup survived node2's restart.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: Both nodes remained on RHEL 7.9 with kernel 3.10.0-1160.el7.x86_64 before and after the work and restarts. The Python 2.7-based resolver ran successfully on that platform without an OS or kernel replacement.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. Direct pre- and post-restart evidence shows persistent DNS service on node1, persistent resolver configuration and successful internal lookup on node2, and preservation of RHEL 7.9 and its installed kernel. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete for both nodes: each has a healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity corroborated by lifecycle snapshots, and recovered task functionality.
limitations: Package-manager consistency observations timed out both before and after execution, so package health could not be independently compared; no package installation or OS/kernel change is shown in the executor timeline.
Lifecycle snapshots do not inspect the contents of the custom resolver or NetworkManager profile; those details are instead established by direct executor commands.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. The resolver files, systemd enablement, and firewall changes in cmd-d3dc971e97cd4833 directly established the node1 outcome; the NetworkManager change in cmd-5357bab01aa24c29 directly established the node2 outcome; and the restart actions in cmd-971c6887587f491c and cmd-716278fb640f4ec6 were bounded evidence-protocol operations. No failed services or unrelated temporary residue were observed afterward.
